objects.description: Typedef for epoch-based time value (seconds since Jan 1, 1970). Only defined here when building for ARDUINO and a libc-provided time_t is not already defined. On other platforms, time_t is expected to come from the C library.
Enumeration indicating the synchronization state of the system time: not set, needs synchronization, or set.
Enumeration of days of the week plus an invalid value. Sunday is the first day.
Enumeration of field indices for time element bytes (second, minute, hour, weekday, day, month, year) plus a count value.
Packed struct holding broken-down time components using 8-bit fields. Year is an offset from 1970 (use provided macros to convert).
Function pointer type for a provider callback that returns current time as time_t with no parameters. Used by setSyncProvider to supply external time source.

functions.name: hour
functions.description: Returns the current hour of day from the library’s maintained time. Intended for retrieving the hour component (24-hour format) of the current clock state.
requirements: none explicitly stated

functions.name: hour
functions.description: Returns the hour of day (24-hour format) from the supplied time value t.
requirements: t is a time value expressed as seconds since Jan 1, 1970 (UNIX epoch), as implied by the library’s time_t usage

functions.name: minute

requirements: none explicitly stated

functions.name: year

requirements: t is a time value expressed as seconds since Jan 1, 1970 (UNIX epoch)

functions.name: now

requirements: none explicitly stated

functions.name: setTime
functions.description: Sets the library’s maintained current time to the supplied epoch time t.
requirements: t must represent seconds since Jan 1, 1970 (UNIX epoch)

functions.name: setTime
functions.signature: void setTime(int hr, int min, int sec, int day, int month, int yr);
functions.description: Sets the library’s maintained current time using separate calendar fields. Exact accepted ranges are not documented here; by convention hr/min/sec/day/month/year form a valid calendar date/time, with month numbering consistent with other APIs (January is 1).
requirements: Parameters must form a valid calendar date/time; precise ranges are not specified in this header
Month numbering is expected to be January=1, consistent with month() documentation
The exact interpretation of yr (full year vs. offset) is not specified here; typical usage is a full four-digit year (unknown in this header)

functions.name: adjustTime
functions.description: Adjusts the maintained current time by the specified number of seconds. Positive values move time forward; negative values move it backward (inferred from name and common usage; exact semantics are not explicitly documented).
requirements: adjustment is interpreted as a number of seconds (inferred)

functions.name: monthStr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a C-string containing the full month name for the given month number. January is month 1 (per documentation of month numbering). The string storage/lifetime is not documented here.
requirements: month uses 1-based numbering with January=1 (per header comments)
Valid input range is not explicitly documented; typical range is 1–12 (unknown if enforced here)

functions.name: dayStr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a C-string containing the full weekday name for the given day code. Sunday is day 1 (per header comments). The string storage/lifetime is not documented here.
requirements: Day-of-week uses 1-based numbering with Sunday=1 (per header comments)
Valid input range is not explicitly documented; typical range is 1–7 (unknown if enforced here)

functions.name: monthShortStr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a C-string containing the abbreviated month name for the given month number. January is month 1. The string storage/lifetime is not documented here.
requirements: month uses 1-based numbering with January=1 (per header comments)
Valid input range is not explicitly documented; typical range is 1–12 (unknown if enforced here)

functions.name: dayShortStr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a C-string containing the abbreviated weekday name for the given day code. Sunday is day 1. The string storage/lifetime is not documented here.
requirements: Day-of-week uses 1-based numbering with Sunday=1 (per header comments)
Valid input range is not explicitly documented; typical range is 1–7 (unknown if enforced here)

functions.name: timeStatus
functions.description: Returns the current time synchronization status: timeNotSet, timeNeedsSync, or timeSet.
requirements: none explicitly stated

functions.name: setSyncProvider
functions.description: Registers an external time provider function used to synchronize the maintained time. The provider must match the getExternalTime signature and return a time_t value when called.
requirements: getTimeFunction must be a valid function pointer of type time_t (*)()
The external provider should return time as seconds since Jan 1, 1970 (UNIX epoch)

functions.name: setSyncInterval
functions.description: Sets the number of seconds between automatic time re-synchronizations with the external provider.
requirements: interval represents a duration in seconds; acceptable ranges/limits are not specified in this header

functions.name: breakTime
functions.description: Decomposes a time_t value into its component fields and stores them into tm (Second, Minute, Hour, Wday, Day, Month, Year). Wday uses Sunday=1 and Year is an offset from 1970 (per struct documentation).
requirements: time is a time value expressed as seconds since Jan 1, 1970 (UNIX epoch)
tm must be a valid, writable reference
Resulting tm.Year is an offset from 1970 (per tmElements_t definition)
Resulting tm.Wday uses Sunday=1 (per tmElements_t comment)

functions.name: makeTime
functions.description: Constructs a time_t value from the provided time elements in tm. tm.Year must be an offset from 1970; Wday uses Sunday=1 (per struct documentation).
requirements: tm must be a valid, initialized set of elements
tm.Year must be the offset from 1970 (not a full year)
tm.Wday uses Sunday=1 (per tmElements_t comment)
Valid ranges for Month/Day/Hour/Minute/Second are not specified in this header
